chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sayyabah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him, saying: 'I am your ransom, we hear people saying that farming is disliked.' So he said to him: 'Farm and plant, by God, people have not done a deed more permissible and more excellent than it. And by God, they will certainly farm crops and plant trees after the emergence of the Dajjal.'
ai.seo_question: Is farming considered disliked or recommended in Shia Islam according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) decisively refutes the notion that agriculture is disliked (makruh), elevating it to a highly virtuous deed that is 'most permissible and purest.' He underscores its enduring significance by noting that farming and planting will persist even after the emergence of the Dajjal, linking agricultural stability to eschatological continuity. This view aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition that views cultivation as a form of worship and a means of sustaining human civilization.
